feed.title: Authorize.Net payment link app — admin panel + hosted payment form (full spec & design provided)
feed.description:
Our company sells premium humidors and cigars. A meaningful share of our orders arrive by email or phone, and we currently have no clean way to take card payment for them.

We need a small, well-built web application in two parts:

1. An internal admin panel where an authorised administrator enters an order number, description, amount and customer email, and sends the customer a secure single-use payment link.

2. A branded hosted payment form where the customer enters their own card and billing address and pays. Processing is through Authorize.Net.

Company staff must never see, type or store card data. We use Accept.js, so the card goes from the customer’s browser straight to Authorize.Net and our server only ever holds an opaque token. Target scope is PCI SAQ A-EP. 

There is a strict three-role model, and it is the core of the project:

Super Admin — creates, blocks and unblocks users. Cannot create payment links.

Administrator — creates and sends payment links. Every link is stamped with their name.

Agent — views payment status and resends a link a customer has lost. Cannot create a link or change an amount.

Role separation must be enforced server-side on every endpoint, not by hiding buttons. 2FA is mandatory for all three roles.

What you get on day one:

A 12-page technical specification: flows, role matrix, field-level validation, data model, gateway configuration, security requirements and acceptance criteria (attached)

Complete UI design for all five screens, in HTML (attached)

All interface copy, error messages and email content

Our Authorize.Net sandbox and production credentials

What we need from you: the build, the gateway integration, hosting setup, security implementation, testing and handover. Nothing to design, nothing to write, nothing to specify.

Stack: your choice, as long as it is mainstream and maintainable — Node/TypeScript, Laravel or Django, with PostgreSQL or MySQL. No Shopify dependency: we run a Shopify store and order numbers come from it, but the order number is typed in by hand and the app must stand alone. Full source code and IP transfer to us on completion.

Please read the attached spec before applying, and answer the screening questions specifically. Generic proposals will not be reviewed.

Scope in one list: Auth: email + password + mandatory TOTP 2FA, self-service password change and reset, Argon2id/bcrypt, breached-password check, lockout, session management

User management (Super Admin only): invite by email — the user sets their own password and 2FA, never an admin; change role; block/unblock with instant session termination; force password reset; reset 2FA; soft delete

Payment link creation (Administrator only): validation, confirmation step, configurable expiry, immutability after send

Payment link list (all roles, actions by role): filters, search, CSV export, detail drawer with attempt history, AVS/CVV results and transaction ID

Hosted payment form: branded, responsive, Accept.js tokenisation, mandatory billing address for AVS, idempotent submission, branded states for expired / paid / cancelled / not found

Authorize.Net: authCaptureTransaction , eCommerce market type, AFDS + AVS + CVV
filters, heldForReview handling, 3DS where the account supports it

Webhooks: signature-verified, idempotent, authoritative for payment status

Transactional email via SendGrid/Postmark/SES: 7 templates, SPF/DKIM/DMARC setup

Audit log: every user and link action with actor, IP and timestamp

Deploy to pay.our-domain, TLS, backups with tested restore, error tracking with card-data scrubbing

Written statement of the PCI SAQ level your architecture achieves

30 days of bug-fix warranty and a recorded handover

Acceptance is objective. The spec lists 17 acceptance criteria. Among them: an Agent session must be rejected when it calls the create-link endpoint directly; double-clicking Pay Now must produce exactly one charge; a deliberately mismatched ZIP must be declined by AVS; a replayed webhook must not duplicate a record; and a network trace must show that no card data ever reaches our server.

Screeneing questions:

1. Have you integrated Authorize.Net before? Which product — Accept.js, Accept Hosted, or the direct API — and please link to a payment page you built that is live today.

2. Walk me through where the card number travels in your proposed architecture, from the customer’s keystroke to Authorize.Net. Be specific about what our server receives.

3. Which PCI SAQ level would your proposed build qualify for, and why?

4. An Agent-role user copies their session token and calls the “create payment link” endpoint directly with curl. What happens, and where in your code is that decided?

5. A customer double-clicks Pay Now and their browser retries the request. Separately, Authorize.Net redelivers the same webhook three times. How does your build avoid a double charge and a duplicate record?

feedback.comment:
Unfortunately, our collaboration with Andrea did not meet the agreed expectations. During the contract, we identified that hours were logged on the project without authorization and while the freelancer was engaged in other tasks unrelated to our project. Once this issue was noticed, we requested a correction and a refund for the affected hours. Only the last week’s charges were eligible for adjustment under Upwork’s rules.

This situation did not align with the level of professionalism and transparency we expect in our ongoing collaborations. Therefore, we decided to end the contract. We hope that this feedback will help improve future working practices.

feedbackToClient.comment:
My experience with this client was challenging, and I would not recommend working with him. From the beginning, he showed inconsistent communication — frequently changing requirements, priorities, and deadlines, which caused confusion and rework.

I consistently maintained a professional approach and completed all assigned tasks, but the client often disregarded results and adjusted expectations without notice. He also imposed unrealistic timelines for complex projects that required detailed analysis and follow-up.

His management style was overly controlling. He requested highly detailed daily reports, reviewed every activity log closely, and questioned completed work that fully met the agreed scope. At times, he modified requirements midway and later questioned the time tracked or the work value, even requesting reviews or returns of already billed time after the tasks were fully completed and approved, without any valid reason.

The client also made unfounded assumptions about my activity despite all work being properly documented through Upwork’s tracker. He reduced weekly hour limits while still expecting full-time results and consistent progress.

In addition, he mentioned performance incentives that were never confirmed and paused the contract unexpectedly. His communication was irregular — alternating between long periods of silence and sudden urgent demands. He showed limited openness to feedback or collaboration, which made the process unnecessarily stressful and unproductive.

Overall, this client demonstrates unrealistic expectations, inconsistent communication, and a lack of understanding of how professional collaboration should work. I recommend documenting everything within the platform, setting clear boundaries, and proceeding with caution.

My experience was demanding and unconstructive, and I would not work with this client again.

Adrian Magnus Humidors Ñ Manual Payment Link System Project Specification for Developers Client: Adrian Magnus Humidors Payment Gateway: Authorize.Net Document version: 1.1 Date: July 2026 Purpose of this document: scope definition and basis for developer quotation 1. Purpose Adrian Magnus Humidors receives a significant portion of its orders manually Ñ customers place orders by email or telephone rather than through the website checkout. Today there is no secure, branded, controlled way to collect card payment for these orders. This project delivers a web application in two parts Payment Link Manager (internal, authenticated) Ñ a back-office panel where authorised staff enter the order details and amount and generate a secure payment link, which is emailed to the customer. Payment Form (public, single-use link) Ñ a branded hosted page where the customer enters their own card details and pays. The transaction is processed through Authorize.Net Two constraints are non-negotiable: Company staff never see, type, store, or transmit card data. The customer always enters their own card. This is a deliberate compliance and liability decision (Section 9). Access to the panel is strictly role-based. Only named, authenticated users may create payment links. See Section 6 Ñ this is the single most important functional requirement of the project. The visual design of both screens is defined in the attached mockup and must be followed.

Scope In scope (Phase 1) Authenticated back-office panel with three-tier role model and user management Payment link generation, expiry, single-use enforcement, status tracking Transactional email delivery of the payment link to the customer Branded hosted payment form with mandatory billing address capture Authorize.Net integration (tokenised card capture, transaction submission, webhooks) Payment result handling, receipt email, internal notification Payment link list view with statuses, resend and cancel actions Full audit log Deployment on an Adrian Magnus subdomain with TLS Sandbox testing and production go-live support Out of scope (Phase 2 candidates Ñ price separately if desired) Shopify / HubSpot order synchronisation (see Section 3) Partial payments, deposits, instalment plans Multi-currency Ñ Phase 1 is USD only Stored cards, recurring billing Refunds and voids from the panel Ñ Phase 1 refunds are handled in the Authorize.Net merchant portal 3. Note on Shopify The company operates a store, and order numbers referenced in payment links will typically originate from Shopify. However, Shopify integration is not a requirement of this project. The system must work as a standalone application . The order number is entered manually by the operator as free text and used only as a human-readable reference on the payment form, in the email, and as passed to Authorize.Net.

Actors Actor Description Owner / Super Admin Company principal. Manages users only. Does not create payment links. Administrator Named staff member. Logs in with own credentials. Creates and sends payment links. Agent Named staff member. Read-only on payment links, plus the ability to resend an existing link. Cannot create anything. Customer Unauthenticated. Receives the link by email and pays. Authorize.Net Payment gateway. Tokenises card data, authorises and captures funds, sends webhooks. 5. End-to-End Flow Customer places an order by email or phone. Staff create the order in the existing internal process (Shopify or otherwise) and obtain an order number An Administrator logs into the panel with their own username and password (plus 2FA). The Administrator enters: Order Number Order Description Amount (USD) Customer Email . Optionally: customer name, internal note, custom expiry. The Administrator clicks Send Payment Link . The system validates the input, creates a record with status , generates a cryptographically random unguessable token, and sends a branded transactional email containing the link. The customer opens the link. The system validates the token (exists, not paid, not cancelled, not expired) and renders the Payment Form showing the order description, order number, product image, and amount. Status

Capability No No No No No The customer enters card details and billing address , ticks the Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy checkboxes, and clicks Pay Now Card data is tokenised in the customerÕs browser, directly by Authorize.Net . The application server receives only an opaque payment token Ñ never the card number or CVV. The server submits the transaction to Authorize.Net (authorise + capture) using the token, the amount, the billing address, and the order number as the invoice reference. On approval: status ; success page displayed with transaction ID; receipt email to the customer; notification email to the internal address; the link is burned and cannot be reused. On decline or error: the customer remains on the form with a clear, non-technical message and may retry. Every attempt is logged. After 5 failed attempts the link is throttled. An Authorize.Net webhook confirms the transaction asynchronously and the system reconciles the record. The webhook, not the browser redirect, is the authoritative source of payment truth. 6.
